mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% indicates tighter monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points over two months signals an improving labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE declines by 0.2pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when RSAFS grows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over a month signals supply chain disruptions, which may lead to decreased economic activity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO declines by 1%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase simultaneously, it indicates a tightening monetary policy combined with labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows while industrial production (INDPRO) declines, it indicates demand outpacing supply, leading to potential inflationary pressures and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when GDPC1 grows and INDPRO declines, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE rises in a late-cycle expansion, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a strong housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when HOUST increases, the hypothesis is rejected.
